mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate of 0.3 percentage points or more signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 6-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces earnings expectations and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods where GDPC1 falls > 2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of 1% or more signals strengthening manufacturing activity, which boosts earnings and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods where INDPRO rises > 1% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate of 0.5 percentage points or more signals a tightening monetary cycle that raises discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods where FEDFUNDS rises > 0.5pp (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) of 1% or more combined with a 3-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) of 5% or more signals weakening demand across consumption and housing, which reduces earnings and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls > 1% in 3 months AND HOUST falls > 5% in 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods where GDPC1 falls > 1% AND HOUST falls > 5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) of 0.3 percentage points or more combined with a 3-month decline in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of 1% or more signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months AND PAYEMS falls > 1% in 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods where UNRATE rises > 0.3pp AND PAYEMS falls > 1% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) of 1% or more combined with a 3-month increase in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) of 2% or more signals weakening demand and rising inflation, which reduces earnings and equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls > 1% in 3 months AND CPIAUCSL rises > 2% in 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods where GDPC1 falls > 1% AND CPIAUCSL rises > 2% (t-test p > 0.05).
